question.problem:
Find, to three decimal places, the interquartile range of the random variable $X$ if the cumulative distribution function of $X$ is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1, \\ \frac{{x}^{2}-1}{8}, & 1\le x\le 3, \\ 1, & x>3.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the interquartile range, we first need to find the lower quartile and the upper quartile.

The lower quartile of a random variable $X$ is the number ${q}_{1}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {q}_{1})=\frac{1}{4},
$$

and the upper quartile is the number ${q}_{3}$ such that

$$
P(X\le {q}_{3})=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

First, we find the lower quartile:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {q}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{4} \\ F({q}_{1}) & =\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{{q}_{1}^{2}-1}{8} & =\frac{1}{4} \\ {q}_{1}^{2}-1 & =2 \\ {q}_{1}^{2} & =3 \\ {q}_{1} & =\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we take the root ${q}_{1}=\sqrt{3}$ because $1\le {q}_{1}\le 3.$

Then, we find the upper quartile:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le {q}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4} \\ F({q}_{3}) & =\frac{3}{4} \\ \frac{{q}_{3}^{2}-1}{8} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ {q}_{3}^{2}-1 & =6 \\ {q}_{3}^{2} & =7 \\ {q}_{3} & =\sqrt{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we take the root ${q}_{3}=\sqrt{7}$ because $1\le {q}_{3}\le 3.$

Therefore, the interquartile range is

$$
\begin{aligned}IQR & ={q}_{3}-{q}_{1} \\  & =\sqrt{7}-\sqrt{3} \\  & ≈0.914\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
